Disclaimer. These data cannot be considered reliable. They are compiled from the TOP500 lists and public sources, and many values (processor and accelerator classification, performance of one device, node counts, everyday devices) are inferred, estimated or approximated. Check the original sources before using them.

Every system published in the TOP500 lists, one row per system (TOP500 system id), with the values of the list where it first appeared: date, Rmax and power at that date. A machine that was upgraded under a new id appears once per id. The processor and accelerator columns show the technologies detected for the timeline (see the methodology). Power is often missing, especially before June 2008. TOP500 publishes no node count: for about 580 of the most powerful systems, the composition of one node (CPU sockets, accelerators) comes from the linked sources. When it gives a whole number, the number of nodes is the TOP500 core count of the entry divided by the cores of one node (CPU cores plus GPU multiprocessors, as TOP500 counts them), which is the size of the machine as benchmarked; otherwise it is the figure of the source. APUs and superchips (MI300A, GH200) count as one socket and one accelerator. In the processor column, the cores per CPU and the frequency come from the TOP500 entry when it gives them; otherwise, marked “≈”, they are those of the reference model of the processor family (see the methodology), as are the vector capabilities. The accelerator details (compute units, CUDA or shader cores, tensor or matrix cores, clock, memory) are those of the reference model of the accelerator family, not of the exact model of each system. The interconnect is read from the TOP500 entry (or deduced from the machine model for early systems); its port bandwidth and usual topology are those of the interconnect family. The price, when it has been published, is the amount reported by the linked source, in its currency and with its scope (contract, budget including operation, extension only…); the dollar figure is a rough conversion for sorting, and prices of different scopes are not directly comparable. The notes say when a composition is inferred. The table is also available as all_systems.csv. Click a column header to sort, click a system name to open its page on top500.org.
